name: Many applicants, few who qualify
what: The posting draws volume but the screen passes almost no one, or passes people who then fail at interview. The evidence points first at the screen itself: exact-match criteria reject qualified candidates (88 percent of employers say so) [44](#cite:44) and the proxies they use are weak predictors (experience-years .07) [1](#cite:1); then at the decision method, since unstructured judgement predicts at .19 and dilutes stronger evidence [1](#cite:1) [8](#cite:8); and then at the validity of whatever assessment is used [32](#cite:32).

reasons.why: the first screen is the usual culprit when volume is high and pass-through is low [44](#cite:44) [1](#cite:1)
if the screen passes people who then fail at interview, the interview may be the unreliable instrument [1](#cite:1) [8](#cite:8) [9](#cite:9)
criteria never tied to the job predict neither who qualifies nor who performs [32](#cite:32)
a cognitively loaded screen used for ranking narrows the pool along group lines as well as ability [1](#cite:1) [32](#cite:32)
for software roles, the live-coding format fails capable candidates [21](#cite:21)

name: Candidates withdraw before a decision
what: Candidates who entered the process stop responding or decline to continue before an offer. In the one large field study, withdrawal tracked perceptions of the organisation and the process, career commitment, current employment, relocation and the views of family and friends, with different reasons at different stages [16](#cite:16); earlier offers were more often accepted [15](#cite:15); 41 percent of organisations reported rising [ghosting](#term:candidate-ghosting) in 2025 [43](#cite:43).

reasons.why: delay between stages, and between final interview and offer, is the modifiable correlate of acceptance [15](#cite:15)
each added stage is a fresh chance to leave; withdrawers differ by stage [16](#cite:16) [14](#cite:14)
the format itself is described as a reason to avoid the process [22](#cite:22)
intrusive or exclusionary questions read as unfair, and [fairness perceptions](#term:applicant-reactions) predict acceptance intentions [14](#cite:14) ([synthesis](#term:synthesis-marker))

name: Few plausible candidates
what: The opening draws too few applicants who could do the job. Among small businesses hiring in September 2026, 87 percent reported few or no qualified applicants [71](#cite:71). The evidence orders the causes: a posting whose title, pay figure or wording sends it to the wrong queue [65](#cite:65) [77](#cite:77); a [credential requirement](#term:degree-requirement) that excludes capable people for almost no validity [1](#cite:1) [68](#cite:68); a reach limited to people who will relocate, now under two percent of job seekers [85](#cite:85); a [referral](#term:referral-hiring) network that is small or all alike [81](#cite:81); an image candidates do not hold [64](#cite:64); and, for [cleared](#term:security-clearance) work, a pool that no one can enter without a [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) [80](#cite:80).

reasons.why: the cheapest and best-evidenced fix: title and pay range decide applicant counts [65](#cite:65) [75](#cite:75)
a degree or years line removes people the [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) would admit [1](#cite:1) [68](#cite:68)
relocation is rare and remote work is valued at 8% of pay; the geography of the posting sets the pool [85](#cite:85) [70](#cite:70)
referrals are the best source and the narrowest [60](#cite:60) [81](#cite:81)
the words and the delivery can exclude without intent [77](#cite:77) [66](#cite:66) [78](#cite:78)
unknown firms are judged on the posting and the recruiter alone [64](#cite:64) [63](#cite:63)
for cleared roles the pool is fixed by prior sponsorship [80](#cite:80)
without source tracking the firm cannot tell which of the above it has [62](#cite:62)

name: Candidates pass but decline the offer
what: The firm wants the candidate and the candidate says no, or says yes and then does not start. The evidence orders the causes: a range held below the market by the labor-category rate [98](#cite:98) [103](#cite:103); a package that looks smaller than a larger employer's once benefits (30 percent of compensation [104](#cite:104)) and arrangements (8 to 20 percent of wages [115](#cite:115)) are counted; an offer process that is slow [15](#cite:15) or anchored on prior pay the law no longer lets the firm use [106](#cite:106); a [counteroffer](#term:counteroffer) or a competing package in the weeks before the start [113](#cite:113) [89](#cite:89); and, for proposed [key personnel](#term:key-personnel-clause), a start date the firm does not control [108](#cite:108). Work conditions and schedules (the matrix's G4 and G6) are adjudicated in sweep 6.

reasons.why: the first thing to check is whether the range can reach the market at all [98](#cite:98) [110](#cite:110)
the comparison the candidate makes includes benefits and arrangements the offer may not state [104](#cite:104) [115](#cite:115)
earlier offers are accepted more often [15](#cite:15)
acceptance is not a start; most managers counter [113](#cite:113)
an offer anchored on prior pay or silent on negotiability drifts into gaps the firm cannot defend [106](#cite:106) [95](#cite:95)
a contingent offer asks the candidate to wait for an award [108](#cite:108)
if the range cannot move, the rate is why [117](#cite:117)

name: Candidates accept but cannot start
what: The offer is accepted and the person is not at work. The evidence puts the causes in an order the firm can check: there was no contract need or [facility clearance](#term:facility-clearance) to [sponsor](#term:clearance-sponsorship) against, so nothing started [119](#cite:119) [120](#cite:120); the investigation is running on [DCSA](#term:dcsa)'s clock, 197 to 243 days on the current figures, against a vacancy that could wait 45 [126](#cite:126) [43](#cite:43); eligibility arrived but the credential, the [reciprocity](#term:reciprocity) decision, the read-in, the [polygraph](#term:polygraph) or the cyber certificate did not [138](#cite:138) [122](#cite:122) [139](#cite:139); the wait itself cost the hire, since each week between acceptance and start raises the odds of a [no-show](#term:new-hire-no-show) by about a fifth [144](#cite:144); there was no funded work for the interval [98](#cite:98) [148](#cite:148); a start-date check surfaced a problem or was taken out of order [128](#cite:128) [130](#cite:130) [136](#cite:136); the hire is a foreign national waiting on an authorization or a visa [132](#cite:132) [142](#cite:142); or the start depends on an award the firm does not control [108](#cite:108). The customer-approval case (the matrix's E5) is adjudicated in sweep 7.

reasons.why: nothing can be requested without a contract need and a facility clearance [119](#cite:119) [120](#cite:120)
the investigation and adjudication run on a clock the firm does not set [126](#cite:126)
the credential, the transfer, the read-in and the certificate are separate decisions by separate owners [138](#cite:138) [122](#cite:122) [139](#cite:139)
each week of waiting raises the odds the hire never starts [144](#cite:144)
the wait is unbillable and sits in the firm's rates [98](#cite:98) [148](#cite:148)
the first three days carry checks that can end the hire [128](#cite:128) [130](#cite:130) [136](#cite:136)
a non-U.S. person needs an authorization before the work and the visa rules are in flux [132](#cite:132) [142](#cite:142)
a proposed key person starts when the award says so [108](#cite:108)

name: Employees start but struggle
what: The hire is at work and not performing. The evidence orders the causes: the adjustment was left to the [newcomer](#term:newcomer-adjustment), with no insider beside them and supervisor support thinning week by week [152](#cite:152) [156](#cite:156) [155](#cite:155); the [ramp](#term:time-to-productivity) is longer than the rate assumed, since output rises for a year where it can be counted [157](#cite:157) [98](#cite:98); the person does not meet the [labor category](#term:labor-category) the slot is billed at, or the customer will not accept them in it [99](#cite:99) [173](#cite:173); the training did not look like the work and did not transfer [162](#cite:162); the senior who should be teaching them is billing elsewhere [158](#cite:158) [99](#cite:99); access to the site, the network or the program is still pending (clear-start) [138](#cite:138); or the selection measured the wrong thing in the first place (select) [1](#cite:1) [7](#cite:7).

reasons.why: structured and social [onboarding tactics](#term:socialization-tactics) predict adjustment, and adjustment predicts performance and staying [152](#cite:152) [155](#cite:155)
output rises steeply through the first year; the rate assumed it was there on day one [157](#cite:157) [98](#cite:98)
the category's qualifications are a contract term enforced by audit [99](#cite:99) [173](#cite:173)
training transfers when it resembles the work and the supervisor expects it used [162](#cite:162)
learning from knowledgeable coworkers is part of the job's value and the seniors are billable [158](#cite:158) [99](#cite:99)
a hire without the badge, the account or the read-in cannot do the work [138](#cite:138)
a screen that did not predict performance let the wrong person through [7](#cite:7)
[unstructured interviews](#term:unstructured-interview) predict performance weakly (.19) [1](#cite:1)

name: Productive employees leave
what: The people the firm most wants to keep are the ones leaving. The evidence orders the causes by the strength of the predictors: they wanted to leave and were looking (ρ .56 and .40), which the firm could have heard [178](#cite:178); pay fell behind peers, new hires or the market, and the comparison, not the level, moved them [182](#cite:182) [92](#cite:92) [93](#cite:93); there was no step up but the wrong one [181](#cite:181) [184](#cite:184); the firm's own manager was absent and the customer's ran the day [178](#cite:178) [183](#cite:183); a vacancy was covered by the remaining staff until the strain showed [178](#cite:178); the job was onsite and fixed while the alternative was not [115](#cite:115) [194](#cite:194); the contract's end was visible and nothing was said [186](#cite:186) [13](#cite:13); a larger employer paid the [external premium](#term:external-hire-premium) for the person the firm trained [93](#cite:93) [187](#cite:187); and the skills were portable because the firm had paid for general ones (develop) [161](#cite:161).

reasons.why: quits follow the comparison with peers and the market, not the level [182](#cite:182) [92](#cite:92)
internal mobility keeps people and the firm has little of it [181](#cite:181)
commitment, fit, satisfaction and the supervisor are the next cluster of predictors [178](#cite:178)
covering a vacancy shows up as stress and role conflict, which predict quitting [178](#cite:178)
the arrangements the job cannot offer are worth a fifth of pay to the median worker [115](#cite:115)
a visible contract end is a [withdrawal cognition](#term:withdrawal-cognitions) with no [right of first refusal](#term:nondisplacement) behind it [178](#cite:178) [186](#cite:186)
external hires are paid about 18% more and [no-poach agreements](#term:no-poach-agreement) are criminal [93](#cite:93) [187](#cite:187)
[general skills](#term:general-human-capital) raise the outside value as fast as the inside [161](#cite:161)
each market-rate hire resets the incumbents' comparison point [93](#cite:93) [92](#cite:92)

name: We approve, the customer rejects
what: The firm's chosen candidate does not survive the customer's review. The evidence and the rules order the causes: the firm and the customer mean different things by qualified, the contract's category line, the evidence's scored assessment and the reviewer's own standard [99](#cite:99) [1](#cite:1) [197](#cite:197); a preference inherited from the customer or the incumbent was written as a requirement no one owns [68](#cite:68) [197](#cite:197); the [requisition](#term:requisition) blended jobs so the candidate fits part of it [65](#cite:65) [99](#cite:99); the customer's review has no clock and the candidate left while it ran [15](#cite:15) [16](#cite:16) [188](#cite:188); the person was a junior in a senior slot [173](#cite:173); the screen measured the wrong thing (select) [7](#cite:7); or the requirements changed during the search [16](#cite:16). Rejections that come back without reasons cannot be acted on, and no study of them was found.

reasons.why: three definitions of qualified, one enforceable, one valid, one decisive [99](#cite:99) [1](#cite:1) [197](#cite:197)
a requirement nobody can trace to the contract or a [job analysis](#term:job-analysis) [68](#cite:68) [32](#cite:32)
the posting described two jobs and the candidate fits one [65](#cite:65) [99](#cite:99)
the review has no period and candidates leave slow processes [188](#cite:188) [15](#cite:15)
the category's qualifications are enforced by audit [173](#cite:173) [99](#cite:99)
the firm's own screen did not predict the work [7](#cite:7)
a proposed person the firm could not deliver is a misrepresentation, not a rejection [203](#cite:203) [108](#cite:108)
